This thread is evidence of why people began referring to global warming as climate change. Global warming means warming on a global scale. If you take the average temperature across all locations on the globe then the average temperature is rising. This is of course still accurate. However, that does not mean that every single place is getting hotter simultaneously. In particular relatively small increases in the average temperature can have enormous climatic changes resulting in record rain in some places, record drought in others, record heat in some, and record cold in others. This is why many indications of unprecedented weather conditions, such as this, are referred to as indicative of climate change or global warming, even though it's quite clearly not becoming warmer in this exact location!
